meta.title: Roadmap: Principia Mathematica in Lean 4
meta.status_source: Statuses are read from the repository at commit efbb89d: docs/PROGRESS.md (whose tables name the commit they measure), docs/PM_CLAIMS.md, docs/STAR9_FOUNDATION.md and data/star9f_ledger.json; counts in the notes are cited with {...} and filled in from those files by scripts/roadmap_chart.py. 'in progress' means some of the task's work is in the repository or under way in the companion text audit.
meta.structure: Four groups, each split into subgroups, each split into leaves (tasks). A leaf is a chapter-sized or stage-sized task.
meta.deps: hard_deps: leaves whose results this leaf's deliverable needs; these edges are the gates. soft_deps: leaves that help (shared infrastructure, comparisons, experience) but are not needed. Dependencies are on particular leaves, not on whole volumes or phases.
meta.order: 'by dependency': the task is placed as early as its hard dependencies allow. 'by choice': it is placed later than they require, after the tasks in placed_after, by the maintainer's order of priorities; order_reason says why. The order is a plan, not a contract: a task that moved records where it was and why in 'moved'.
meta.prior_work: The first step of every task is a search for prior work, with several independent search tools whose findings are compared. Each entry has an evidence level: 'measured' (its source was read at a pinned commit; nothing was built unless said), 'documented' (a paper or README says so), 'unverified' (reported, not checked), or 'from memory' (listed before the search reached this task). 'effect' says what the search found it good for: reuse (licensed code or data to import or depend on), ideas (read it, write our own), check against (an independent result to compare with), nothing found, or not yet searched. 'Not found' means not found by the searches so far, not that nothing exists. Code is never copied from unlicensed sources.
meta.sizes: S: days to a few weeks; M: weeks to a few months; L: several months or more.
meta.overview_alt: Roadmap overview: four groups of work (PM itself; checking underneath; comparing across; results about PM) and five milestones (Vol I checked, Vol II checked, Vol III checked, first edition audited, Lean's kernel fragment verified)
meta.readme_intro: The work is split into four groups that run side by side. Each group is split into subgroups, and each subgroup into chapter-sized or stage-sized tasks. Every task starts with a search for prior work. Open a group below to see its tasks. The full plan, including the reason each task waits (a dependency or a choice), the prior work found for it and the tasks that moved, is in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md), with the [dependency view](docs/ROADMAP.md#dependency-view).

leaves.size_reason: The dot parser and the completeness theorem exist; the task runs them on the raw transcription as a standing check and reports each failure to the text audit.
leaves.status_note: PM/Statements.lean was generated from the transcription by a dot parser (scripts/gen_lean.py), and ✱1·4 and ✱4·42 were found this way; not yet a standing check. It catches underivable transcriptions only: a derivable formula can still be mistranscribed.

prior_work.note: The text audit sets PM's dots aside; this check is what the formalization adds.

leaves.name: Adequacy, stage 1: ✱1–✱5, a finite certificate format and both translations
leaves.size_reason: Propositional formulas are already finite; the work is the certificate format and both translations.

prior_work.note: Propositional formulas have no binders; none needed.

leaves.name: Adequacy, stage 2: a finite first-order core for ✱9–✱14, with derivations as data, and the easy direction (every core derivation gives a QThm theorem)
leaves.size_reason: Finite syntax with named or de Bruijn variables, types and orders; finite derivations; a translation into QF and soundness at every V.
leaves.status_note: Today `QF` binds with Lean functions and `QThm.gen` takes one premise for every variable, so a `QThm` proof is not a finite object (docs/SEMANTICS.md). The core is the source for pm.mm beyond ✱5, the Rocq re-check and incompleteness.

prior_work.note: Two independent searches recommend this architecture: a finite core as the source of truth, related to the present encoding by a proved translation.

known.work: FormalizedFormalLogic/Foundation (Apache-2.0): locally nameless first-order formulas
HOL_in_HOL_Deep (BSD): a locally nameless deep embedding
lean-hoas: in Lean, a parametric encoding does not exclude exotic terms; no license, ideas only
Grenrus (2025, Agda): a well-formedness predicate and a proved round trip between de Bruijn and parametric terms; no license
Hybrid (Isabelle): an encoding over de Bruijn terms with an admissibility predicate and adequacy results
Nothing for ramified types, or for derivations with an infinitary generalization rule

leaves.name: Adequacy, stage 2, the converse: from QThm back to the finite core
leaves.size_reason: Exotic intermediate formulas, the infinitary generalization rule and order side conditions; no precedent found. Possibly research-level.
leaves.status_note: Three ways, to be chosen before incompleteness starts: (a) a restricted QThm whose formulas are all well-formed; (b) the theorems needed re-derived in the core; (c) full conservativity.

leaves.name: Adequacy, stage 3: classes and beyond

prior_work.note: Foundation's theorems are stated for first-order theories, hence the first-order presentation.

established: ✱1–✱5: {progress:✱1–✱5} numbered assertions derived from ✱1·1–✱1·6, and ✱1–✱5 complete for two-valued truth tables.

Vol I: {progress:Vol I} numbered assertions proved (✱1–✱5 from ✱1·1–✱1·6; from ✱9 on, from the primitive propositions of ✱10's method and ✱12·1, ✱12·11), as counted in docs/PROGRESS.md at commit {progress-commit}. Vols II and III are not started.

✱9 by its own method (PM/Found9): {star9f} numbered ✱9 propositions proved; ✱9·31 is open under the definitions as printed. Every ✱9 theorem is a ✱10 theorem given a variable of every type; the converse is proved given Rep and a variable of every type.
Every class and relation expression that PM's notation forms is extensional (pp. 200, 213).
No PM derivation depends on any Lean axiom; consistency is shown in a finite model, at the model's variables.
PM's claims, with their status, are in PM_CLAIMS.md. {claims-counts}
Known limits: no adequacy theorem yet (the formula type has terms that match no finite PM formula, and a `QThm` proof is not a finite object); the models forget orders.
